about: The listeners' hit rule (#1562), run by the C# ListenerHits (ListenerHitsFixtureTests) and by the TypeScript listenerHits (listener-hits.spec.ts). Each case is what lies under one point, in paint order: an entry painted later is above the ones before it, and an entry's children are inside it. A listener has a behavior; a solid draws or answers. hear lists the ids of the listeners that hear, in the order they are told.

cases.name: a deferring listener hears what lands on the text it holds
a deferring listener hears nothing in the gap of the column it holds
an opaque listener hears in the gap of the column it holds
a translucent listener hears in the gap of the column it holds
a deferring listener hears in a gap over a fill its child draws
nested deferring listeners over a text both hear, the inner first
an opaque inner listener over empty space is the outer one's child hit
a translucent inner listener over empty space is not the outer one's child hit
a translucent listener over empty space lets the listener behind it hear
an opaque listener over empty space hides the listener behind it
a deferring listener over empty space is passed over for the listener behind it
a translucent listener whose child is hit hides the listener behind it
something drawn above a listener, outside it, hides it
empty space above a listener, outside it, hides nothing
a fill behind a listener, around it, hides nothing
two translucent listeners over a deferring one, all over empty space: the two hear, the topmost first
